A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

human lymphocytes can be divided into at least three populations, namely: (1) B lymphocytes; (2) T lymphocytes; and (3) a third population which is not yet characterized but which includes null cells and monocytes.
human B lymphocytes can be identified by a specific heterologous anti-B-lymphocyte antiserum and that they can be separated from T lymphocytes, monocytes and null cells.
